gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu sits with its midline held high and its counters left connected to the outside, easy and unfussy. Nordic above it is the opposite: a heavy, ancient display voice.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Nordic spaces its letters like brush dabs set far apart. Noto Sans Thaana answers with wide channels into each counter and big open lowercase forms, which loosens the tight, closed heading above.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai swells its lowercase like inflated glass beads, with rounded letters left open and approachable. Nordic is the tighter one, best at closed, powerful shapes while the body does its friendly opening up.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall bodies that make its lowercase look bold, with spacious gaps at the curve ends. Noto Sans Thai Looped feels airy beside Nordic, whose stems match its hairlines because it has none.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Nordic holds every stroke as constant as bent wire, its letters closed and ancient, while Noto Sans Tifinagh stays open and rounded beneath it. They feel like carved stone beside soft clay.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Cut-back terminals, big gaps, tall letters. Nordic is best at joints where strokes meet without thinning or bulging, while Noto Sans Tirhuta is best at its dominant x-height and open, contemporary sans-serif terminals.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic keeps almost no gap between x-height and cap height, its letter mouths open like a chalk arc left unjoined. Noto Sans Ugaritic is the friendly sans-serif here, while Nordic does the powerful work with no brush-style swell at all.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-vai: Nordic is closed, powerful and ancient. Noto Sans Vai does what the heading can't, making words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space between curve ends and the stem.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Nordic brings a cramped, ancient weight, its letters closed like a pressed leaf fold. Noto Sans Vithkuqi is better at openness, with throats on a, c, e and s and only a minimal step from cap to lowercase.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Hulking, chalk-thick lowercase meets a wire-bent sign look. Nordic holds constant thickness throughout while Noto Sans Wancho pushes its e wide open at the terminal. Paragraphs would read broad and sturdy.
